# Synthetic Temporal replay histories

These JSON files are compatibility baselines generated by the real time-skipping
server with production workflows and in-memory stub activities. They contain
synthetic identifiers only. No operator database, provider, Docker or credentials
are used. Normal tests replay these files and never overwrite them.

To record an initial baseline into an empty corpus:

```sh
npm run temporal:record-histories -w @space/worker
npm test -w @space/worker
```

To add histories for a reviewed `patched()` workflow change, use a new version
label (lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens):

```sh
npm run temporal:record-histories -w @space/worker -- --version goal-v2
npm test -w @space/worker
```

Before running recording scenarios, the recorder replays every existing history
against the current workflow bundle and stops on any failure. New histories use
names such as `dot-wake-signals--goal-v2.json`. Existing files are never replaced;
a reused version/name fails. The original filenames and older patched-branch
histories remain part of subsequent replay tests. Normal tests do not record.

For an isolated recorder check, copy the existing JSON corpus to a temporary
directory and add `--output-dir /absolute/path/to/copied-corpus` to the recording
command. Both the pre-recording replay and the final replay then use that copy;
the final replay covers its retained and newly added histories. This option does
not redirect ordinary test runs away from the committed baseline. Inspect the
new histories before deliberately adding an approved patched version to Git.

After the initial baseline, re-recording is allowed only together with a reviewed
`patched()` workflow change. Preserve histories for older branches while adding
new ones. Never re-record a failing history to make a replay incompatibility pass.

The test-only legacy bundle selects the existing pre-patch branches without
emitting patch markers. Its recorded histories are then replayed with the
unmodified current workflow source. The negative bundle adds one timer to
`dotGoalWorkflow`; a test requires a `DeterminismViolationError`, proving the gate
can detect an incompatible change. Neither variant is used by production workers.
